svg.title: Infection and response overview
svg.desc: Pathogens cause disease: Bacteria may release toxins; viruses reproduce inside cells. Fungi and protists also cause disease. Spread: contact, water, air, food or vectors. Hygiene, isolation, vaccination and vector control break routes. Named human infections: Measles: droplets, fever/rash. HIV: body fluids, damages immune cells; antiretrovirals control it. Salmonella: food, gut illness. Gonorrhoea: sexual contact, discharge/pain; antibiotic resistance matters. Malaria: protist carried by mosquitoes; recurrent fever. Nets and breeding control reduce spread. Defence & vaccination: Skin, mucus/cilia and stomach acid form barriers. White cells engulf pathogens, make antibodies and antitoxins. Vaccination → specific antibodies/memory → faster later response. High uptake reduces transmission. Medicines & targeting: Antibiotics treat bacteria, not viruses. Painkillers treat symptoms. Trials check toxicity, efficacy and dose. Monoclonals: lymphocyte + tumour cell → hybridoma → clone. Specific binding enables tests and targeted treatments; side effects remain. Plant problems: TMV: mosaic leaves; black spot: fungal spots/leaf loss. Both reduce photosynthesis. Aphids feed on sap. Nitrate shortage → less protein/growth; magnesium shortage → less chlorophyll/chlorosis. Identify using symptoms, references, labs or antibody tests. Plant protection: Cell walls, waxy cuticle and shedding bark resist entry. Antibacterial chemicals attack bacteria; poisons, thorns and hairs deter feeding. Drooping/curling leaves and mimicry discourage herbivores.
